Lesson 058: thermal throttling and battery

    What this shows

    Phones can't keep their top speed

    A phone can sprint, but it can only cool a couple of watts for long. Above that it heats up and then lowers its own clocks.

    Energy per frame is the real budget

    Sustained frame rate = the power the phone can cool ÷ the energy one frame costs. Make frames cheaper, or make fewer of them.

    Adapt before the phone does

    A game that lowers its own render scale a little keeps a steady frame rate. A phone that throttles for you changes clocks, and frames become uneven.

    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 058's numbers: display, radio and audio 1.6 W; the chip uses 77 mJ a frame at full quality and 46 mJ on the mobile tier; the phone can cool 2.2 W of chip power for as long as you like and holds 19.2 watt-minutes of extra heat before throttling; throttled clocks use 25% less energy per frame; adaptive quality may cut a frame's energy by up to 25%; a 15.4 Wh battery.
